headline: OpenAI's $50 billion revenue report sends AI stocks lower
dek: OpenAI's figure is below the $68 billion reported earlier, and Nvidia, Oracle and CoreWeave fell, per CNBC and SiliconANGLE.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A lower number moves the market
body: OpenAI told investors its annualized revenue reached about $50 billion at the end of September, below the $68 billion widely reported before (CNBC, SiliconANGLE).
Shares tied to AI infrastructure fell on Thursday. CoreWeave dropped nearly 8%, and Nvidia, Oracle, AMD, Broadcom, Intel and Super Micro Computer also declined (CNBC, SiliconANGLE).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Gross versus net revenue
s3.body: The gap comes from how revenue is counted, according to a person familiar with the matter (CNBC).

points.t: The $68 billion included gross revenue from OpenAI's partners, which allowed a closer comparison with Anthropic (CNBC).
The $50 billion reflects net revenue, the amount left after what goes to partners (CNBC).
OpenAI cited 77% total run-rate growth in the third quarter and 107% for its enterprise business (CNBC, SiliconANGLE).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Valuations rest on revenue
body: OpenAI is under pressure to justify its $852 billion valuation before a widely expected IPO, an initial public offering of shares (CNBC, SiliconANGLE).
Oracle's fall drew attention because it holds multibillion-dollar contracts with OpenAI (SiliconANGLE). The Nasdaq fell 1.25% on the day (SiliconANGLE).

items.t: OpenAI filed its prospectus confidentially in June and has signaled a 2027 debut (CNBC, SiliconANGLE).
Anthropic could go public as soon as November 9, according to reports cited by SiliconANGLE.
OpenAI is in early talks on a round of about $30 billion; no term sheet is final (CNBC).

caption.hook: OpenAI told investors its revenue is $50 billion, and AI stocks fell on Thursday, per CNBC and SiliconANGLE.
body: Analyst Holger Mueller of Constellation Research told SiliconANGLE the episode shows investors need to do more research into the AI industry's finances before trusting market valuations.
In September, chief executive Sam Altman said the moment was ill-advised for an IPO, citing AI safety concerns. CNBC adds that OpenAI pulled its GPT-6.1 Astra launch for missing safety standards.
Anthropic is also preparing an IPO and reportedly seeks a $2 trillion valuation. In August it told investors its run rate topped $65 billion (CNBC, SiliconANGLE).
caption.cta: Which matters more when comparing AI companies: gross revenue or net revenue?
